mission: LÉLU 2.2.2 — memory lifecycle and deletion validation
method: in-process, the same store and workspace APIs the runtime uses; no mocks for deletion itself

scenarios.evidence: tests/context-sovereignty.test.ts — the memory's workspace observation (linked by memoryId) is removed with it; the text no longer appears in workspaceItems
new test: only the deleted observation goes, the rest of the workspace is intact, second delete is a no-op
observations filed in that conversation are removed; memory deletion rules from M22/M22.1 still apply
session-local observations are readable only in their own session (test W); a new session sees none
agent observations are filed in the run's conversation; a removed task leaves no ownerless event that any scope renders (execution events require owner match)
new test: old text is removed, replacement keeps provenance, old text cannot be quoted

a removed project no longer appears in the snapshot, checkpoints or project sections; its conversation-filed observations go with their conversation. Project-associated observations are not a separate store (no duplicate memory system).

non_survival.workspace_labels: text removed; name/count remains but count is a number, not the content
non_survival.cognitive_snapshots: assembled fresh per turn from live state, never cached across turns
non_survival.agent_caches: none: agent context is built for the invocation
non_survival.provider_payloads: built per request; deletion before a request removes the text from that request

limits: A payload already sent to a provider before deletion cannot be recalled; deletion is validated at assembly time, before the request.
Durable memories are preserved when a conversation is deleted, as M22 requires; their provenance remains.
